title: DRBench Pro Caps Top Research Agent at 57% Coverage
summary: DRBench Pro benchmark shows best deep-research agent hits 57.04% knowledge coverage across 144 tasks and 44,102 rubrics in 24 domains.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- DRBench Pro benchmark, released November 26, 2026, evaluates deep-research agents on structured knowledge coverage rather than final-answer quality alone.
- The best-performing agent across 16 tested systems achieved 57.04% overall coverage, measured as the geometric mean of breadth and depth.
- The benchmark uses 144 cases spanning 24 domains and 44,102 evidence-grounded rubrics built from Wikipedia-derived knowledge trees to score agents.


A new benchmark for[deep-research agents](https://emergent.sh/glossary/deep-research-agent) shows the top-performing system covers just 57.04% of relevant knowledge across 144 multi-domain tasks. DRBench Pro, introduced in an arXiv paper on November 26, 2026, shifts evaluation away from subjective report quality toward structured, evidence-grounded coverage metrics. The benchmark tested 16 agents using 44,102 rubrics derived from Wikipedia knowledge trees spanning 24 domains.


## How DRBench Pro Measures Coverage


Traditional benchmarks assess final-answer quality along dimensions like coherence and relevance. The DRBench Pro authors argue that approach misses a critical question: which research directions does an agent explore, and how deeply? Each rubric in the benchmark corresponds to a relation in a knowledge tree, letting evaluators measure both breadth across major topics and depth along related chains of reasoning. The overall coverage score is the geometric mean of breadth and depth, ensuring agents cannot compensate for shallow exploration by casting a wide net.


The 144 test cases draw from 24 domains, with rubrics grounded in Wikipedia-derived evidence. The paper reports that rubric judgments align closely with human annotations, and agent rankings remain stable across different metric configurations. This design aims to offer a reproducible standard for measuring long-horizon research performance.


## Release Date and Availability


DRBench Pro was officially released on November 26, 2026, via arXiv. The paper does not name the specific agent that achieved the 57.04% coverage ceiling, nor does it detail how far behind the other 15 tested systems fell. The authors present the benchmark as a stable evaluation tool for both academic labs and commercial teams building deep-research agents.


## Performance Context and Agent Landscape


The 57% coverage mark places deep-research agents well below human-level knowledge synthesis. Recent agent evaluations show similar ceilings: earlier benchmarks reported top systems clearing just 60% of tasks in domain-specific suites. The DRBench Pro results suggest that expanding both breadth and depth simultaneously remains a bottleneck for current architectures.


The benchmark arrives alongside a cluster of agent-evaluation papers this week, including CARE-OPD on SWE-bench Verified and SPLICE on agent reinforcement learning. Each highlights a different dimension of agent capability, from code generation to multi-turn decision-making. DRBench Pro focuses specifically on structured knowledge coverage in long-horizon research runs.


## Implications for Research and Development


The 44,102 rubrics and Wikipedia grounding give teams a granular view of where agents succeed and fail. If breadth scores lag, an agent may miss entire research directions; if depth scores lag, it may skim topics without following chains of reasoning. The benchmark's stability across metric configurations means teams can compare results over time without worrying about shifting baselines.


For organizations deploying deep-research agents in[legal](https://emergent.sh/ai-agent-builder/legal-research) ,[scientific](https://emergent.sh/ai-agent-builder/scientific-research) , or[market](https://emergent.sh/ai-agent-builder/market-research) contexts, the 57% ceiling underscores the need for human oversight. The gap between current coverage and comprehensive knowledge synthesis remains wide, and production systems will likely need hybrid workflows that combine agent exploration with expert review.


## What This Means


DRBench Pro offers the research community a reproducible, knowledge-centric standard for evaluating deep-research agents. The 57.04% coverage result confirms that state-of-the-art systems still leave nearly half of relevant knowledge on the table, even when given structured tasks and evidence-grounded rubrics. Teams building or deploying these agents now have a clearer benchmark for tracking incremental progress in both breadth and depth, and a sharper picture of where current architectures fall short.
